name: wide_param
hypothesis: Base LONG VWAP mean-reversion has a profitable parameter region missed by the narrow default search.
notes: WIDE random search over a 120-sample of a 26,880-combo grid (entry_dist x vol_mult x max_hold x vwap_exit_band x stop_loss); 120 unique configs evaluated. Tuned on TRAIN, selected the single best by VAL net total_pnl under train>=30/val>=15 trade guards, then evaluated TEST exactly once. TRAIN ret=-0.09752 (n=936, pnl=-9.75), VAL ret=+0.04154 (n=244, pnl=+4.15), TEST ret=+0.15048 (n=209, pnl=+15.05). NEGATIVE-EDGE VERDICT despite a positive raw TEST number: (1) the selected config LOSES money in-sample (TRAIN pnl=-9.75) — a config that doesn't work on TRAIN but 'wins' OOS is the textbook overfit/regime artifact, not edge (inverted, non-sane train->test gap). (2) Regime-luck audit: 72% of ALL 120 tried configs are positive on this TEST window (even the narrow default base config is positive on TEST while losing on TRAIN+VAL), and 0 of 120 configs are positive on ALL THREE splits — so TEST positivity is a property of a favorable test regime (2026-04-10..2026-06-03), not of any discovered edge. Conclusion: the hypothesis is FALSE — there is no profitable, robust parameter region for the base LONG VWAP mean-reversion after costs on this thin IEX data; the apparent OOS gain is regime luck, so survives_oos=False.
